items.title: Albert Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: you’re going to give up a Rembrandt for that?

ctx.x: We seem to be in a hurry to change.

But that’s advertising that’s doing it. The guys got all that stuff in a warehouse and he’s trying to sell it. That’s basically what that is. So he goes to make you dissatisfied. Now he’s already selling you something with a lifetime guarantee. So now he wants to make you dissatisfied so he can sell you something else. That’s his problem. But in the arts you don’t do that you see? The older the thing is, the better. Here’s the newest thing in painting — you’re going to give up a Rembrandt for that?

Don’t think so. Well we have a couple of minutes before I know you have to move on. And I wanted to read one thing in your book from Basie, and just have you comment on it. This is something he said: “it’s the way you play it that makes it. What I say for Christ’s sakes, you don’t have to kill yourself to swing. Play like you play, play like you think, and then you got it, if you’re going to get it, and whatever you get, that’s you so that’s your story.” That was pretty much his philosophy on playing? That you…
